builtin_inventory: Bodies with status='hypothetical' in star_analysis/data/builtin_systems.py: Planet Nine (Sun), Alpha Centauri Ab (orbits Alpha Centauri A), Proxima Centauri c (in both _alpha_centauri and _proxima_centauri) and 55 Cnc g (already Unconfirmed row 42), plus two stars with hypothetical orbits (Proxima Centauri around A; 55 Cancri B). coverage.result: 2 candidates (Proxima Cen c ambiguous; alf Cen A b ambiguous)
coverage.notes: Proxima b and d are confirmed and on the sheet. NIRPS 2025 (A&A 700, A11) refines the Msini of b to 1.055 +/- 0.055 M_E and of d to 0.260 +/- 0.038 M_E; the sheet has 1.05 and 0.26, so no change is needed. NIRPS 2025 also notes a 2.91 d FIP peak below the 10% threshold; it is not claimed as a planet and was not added. alpha Cen Bb is refuted (Rajpaul+2016). Demory+2015 report a single HST transit-like event around alpha Cen B; see considered_not_added. The Gratton+2020 SPHERE source is a proposed counterpart of Proxima c and is folded into that record. No candidate around alpha Cen B was found. For the JWST re-observation of alf Cen A planned for August 2026, no published result was found as of 2026-09-24. exoplanet.eu was tried (catalog/?query=Proxima) but the page returned a query syntax error; not retried, for budget.

candidates.tier_reason: A published RV candidate (K = 1.2 +/- 0.4 m/s, ~3 sigma, e fixed at 0) that later work contests and has never recovered. Artigau+2022's LBL reanalysis of HARPS rejects models with c by BIC and traces the signal to HARPS-TERRA systematics. NIRPS+HARPS+ESPRESSO (Suarez Mascareno+2025) do not detect it significantly: a guided fit gives K = 58 +/- 28 cm/s, about half the published amplitude, at P = 1800 d. The astrometric support (Kervella+2020 Gaia DR2 PMa; Benedict & McArthur 2020 HST FGS; Libralato+2025 HST+Gaia) is low-significance and model-dependent, and Gratton+2020's SPHERE counterpart was not confirmed by its own authors. Not formally refuted, but the best current reading leans toward 'unlikely'. Kept as 'ambiguous' because the brief names it as the contested example; the writer may downgrade it.

candidates.orbit_flags: RV only; eccentricity fixed at 0; the baseline covers about one orbit. The period is the Damasso+2020 posterior (1900 d); the 5.21 yr in their abstract comes from the same fit. The alternative astrometric solutions depend on their models. Benedict & McArthur 2020 (FGS+RV+SPHERE): P = 1928 +/- 20 d, i = 133 +/- 1 deg, Omega = 331 +/- 1 deg, true mass 7 +/- 1 M_E in their Table 1 but 6 +/- 1 M_E in their text (the note contradicts itself), and the fit leans on the unconfirmed Gratton+2020 SPHERE source. Kervella+2020: i = 152 +/- 14 deg, m = 12 +12/-5 M_E. NIRPS 2025 sees at most a lower-amplitude signal at ~1800-2000 d. Not in the NASA Exoplanet Archive; the OEC still lists it as confirmed.

candidates.designation: S1 (Beichman et al. 2025, Table 2), treated as the same object as the NEAR candidate C1 (Wagner et al. 2021)
candidates.tier_reason: A single-epoch, single-roll JWST/MIRI detection (S/N 4-6, 3.3-4.3 sigma), not recovered in February or April 2025. Its authors flagged the 2019 NEAR detection C1 as possibly an instrumental artefact. That S1 and C1 are the same object is an assumption, and only 52% of the stable S1+C1 orbits are consistent with both non-detections. The authors call it 'at the moment, a planet candidate'. No published result from the planned August 2026 re-observation was found.

candidates.designation: Planet Nine (Batygin & Brown 2016); parameters as updated by Brown, Holman & Batygin 2024
candidates.tier_reason: No signal of any kind has been detected. The planet is a pure dynamical inference from TNO orbital clustering and is included only because it is a built-in viewer body. The clustering itself is disputed: Napier+2021 find the ETNO sample consistent with no clustering, and Siraj+2025 find ~3 sigma clustering in varpi but prefer a different, smaller planet (0.06% overlap with the BB21 population). In support, BB21 find the clustering significant at 99.6%, and Batygin+2024 reject a P9-free model at ~5 sigma for low-i Neptune-crossers. Direct searches (ZTF, DES, Pan-STARRS1) have excluded 78% of the BB21 parameter space. 'ambiguous' reflects a live, unresolved debate; 'unlikely' is also defensible.
candidates.detection_method: Dynamical inference (clustering of distant TNO orbits); not detected

a_au.where: final section: updated from the surviving members of the P9 reference population

candidates.orbit_flags: Inferred, not observed. Chosen: Brown, Holman & Batygin 2024, the originators' latest update, which is the BB21 posterior conditioned on the ZTF/DES/PS1 non-detections: a 500 +170/-120 AU, m 6.6 +2.6/-1.7 M_E, aphelion 630 +290/-170 AU, current distance 550 +250/-180 AU, V ~22.0. They state the other parameters are 'generally unchanged' from BB21: i 16 +/- 5 deg, perihelion 300 +85/-60 AU (BB21 abstract). No eccentricity or period is published as a value; the writer may derive e from q and the aphelion if wanted (orange border). Earlier estimates: BB16 nominal a 700 AU, e 0.6, i 30, omega 150, m 10 M_E; Batygin+2019 ranges m 5-10 M_E, a 400-800 AU, e 0.2-0.5, i 15-25 deg.
candidates.reference: Batygin & Brown 2016, AJ 151, 22 (proposal); Brown & Batygin 2021, AJ 162, 219 (orbit fit); Brown, Holman & Batygin 2024, arXiv:2401.17977 (update, final section)
